hypothesis: If the Glacial period was globally simultaneous, then the glacial maxima recorded in independent globally distributed marine oxygen-isotope records (which integrate global ice volume and deep-water temperature) coincide in time across ocean basins, giving a coherent, high-amplitude signal of colder-than-present global conditions in the Pleistocene.
pass_criterion: In the LR04 stack, benthic d18O at the glacial maxima of MIS 2, 6 and 12 exceeds the Holocene (0-10 ka mean) value by at least 1.0 per mil, and the stack's reported standard error at those maxima is below 0.1 per mil. If per-site records from the 57 sites are also checked, at least 80% place their MIS 2, 6 and 12 maxima within +/-5 kyr of the stack maximum.
fail_criterion: The 0-1.0 Ma glacial/interglacial d18O amplitude of the stack is below 0.5 per mil, or fewer than 50% of sites place their MIS 2, 6 and 12 maxima within +/-5 kyr of the stack maximum.
interpretation: Darwin's 'Glacial period' is read as the Pleistocene glacial stages (marine isotope stages with high benthic d18O). 'Temperature of the whole world simultaneously cooler' is operationalised as synchronous high benthic d18O (ice volume plus deep-ocean cooling) across globally distributed sites. Caveat: the LR04 age model aligns records to each other and to orbital targets, so synchrony is partly built in. The test is therefore weak on timing and stronger on coherence of amplitude. Darwin's 'at least in part' and 'broad longitudinal belts' are modernly read as a global ocean signal, not terrestrial glacier advance dates. A decisive test of glacial-advance timing itself would need independently dated moraine data.

dataset.name: Pliocene-Pleistocene stack of globally distributed benthic stable oxygen isotope records
dataset.why_it_fits: Publicly downloadable tab-delimited series (CC BY 3.0) built from 57 globally distributed benthic d18O records. Fields used are age (ka), benthic d18O (per mil) and its standard error, plus the sedimentation-rate and age-model appendices. These allow checking the synchrony and amplitude of the global glacial signal.
